sections.title: What are POIs?
sections.content: A Point of Information (POI) is a question or short statement directed at the speaker during their speech. POIs are a key tool for engaging with opponents, testing their arguments, and showing your command of the topic.
bullets: POIs must be concise — usually 15 seconds max
They are offered during GSL speeches, not during caucus
A strong POI can derail a weak speaker's entire argument

sections.title: How to Offer a POI
sections.content: To offer a POI, stand up or raise your placard when the speaker invites POIs. The chair will recognize you. Keep your POI focused and direct.
bullets: Do not make a speech disguised as a question
Reference something the speaker just said to show you are listening

sections.feedback: Effective POIs are short, relevant, and force the speaker to respond to a specific weakness.

sections.q: When during a committee session can POIs be offered?
options: During GSL speeches when the speaker accepts them
At any time by standing up
sections.explain: POIs are offered during GSL speeches. The speaker decides whether to accept or decline.

sections.statement: A POI should be a short speech presenting your own argument.
sections.feedback: A POI is a question or short challenge, not a speech. Making a speech disguised as a POI is against procedure.

sections.sentence: A POI stands for Point of {0}.

sections.instruction: What is wrong with this POI?
sections.argument: During a speech about climate change policy, a delegate stands up and says: 'Actually, I would like to point out that our country has done more than yours — we signed the Paris Agreement, we reduced emissions, we invested in renewables, and we are currently leading the global transition. Your entire argument is wrong.'
options: The POI is too long — it is a speech, not a question
The POI attacks the speaker personally
The POI does not reference climate change
There is nothing wrong with it
sections.feedback: This is a speech disguised as a POI. A POI should be a concise question or short challenge (under 15 seconds), not a full counter-speech.

questions.q: What should you do if you receive a strong POI you cannot answer?
options: Acknowledge it honestly and pivot to your main argument
Ask the chair to rule it out of order
questions.feedback: Acknowledge the point briefly and pivot. Judges respect honesty over evasion.
